review_notes: I read the whole file. It has four helper lemmas in the namespace WAnchor and one very large theorem, `solution`. The file declares no simp lemmas, simp attributes, simp sets or simp-normal-form conventions. Every `simp` and `simp only` call uses an explicit lemma list or very short argument lists. The only existing simp lemma it relies on is `ModularCurve.coeffMap_coeff`, which is `@[simp]` in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_LaurentCoeff.lean, and it points the right way (it unfolds a coefficient of a mapped series). I found no candidate for a missing canonical simp lemma, no wrongly oriented rewrite, no competing rules and no credible loop. Lemmas such as `coeffMap_injective`, `exists_ringHom_coeffMap_comp_eq`, `baseChange_induction` and `exists_finset_of_baseChange` are used by name or as explicit arguments, so putting `@[simp]` on them would not help. A grep suggests `coeffMap_injective` also exists in Theorems/Thm_ModularCurve_coeffMap_injective.lean. That is duplication, not a simp-interface issue, so it falls outside this rubric. I did not check every downstream use of the namespace, so a missed use is the only remaining uncertainty.
